'''Chinmoy Sankar Dey''' (born 18 March 1961) is an Indian [[molecular biologist]] and a professor at ''Kusuma School of Biological Sciences'' of the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi]]. Known for his research on [[insulin resistance]], Dey's is a J. C. Bose National Fellow of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] and an elected fellow of the  [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and the [[Indian National Science Academy]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards for his contributions to Medical Sciences in 2003. He is also a recipient of the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]] of the [[Department of Biotechnology]].

== Biography ==
[[File:University of Calcutta cropped.JPG|thumb|235px|University of Calcutta]]
S. C. Dey was born on 18 March 1961 in [[Kolkata]], the capital of the Indian state of [[West Bengal]].<ref name="Faculty Profile A">{{Cite web |url=http://bioschool.iitd.ac.in/csdeycvfeb2017.pdf |title=Faculty Profile A |date=2017 |publisher=Bioschool, IIT Delhi |access-date=26 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170327081309/http://bioschool.iitd.ac.in/csdeycvfeb2017.pdf |archive-date=27 March 2017 }}</ref> He graduated in zoology from the [[University of Calcutta]] in 1982 and continued at the institution to obtain a master's degree in 1984.<ref name="Faculty Profile B">{{Cite web |url=http://bioschool.iitd.ac.in/CSD.html |title=Faculty Profile B |date=2017 |publisher=Bioschool, IIT Delhi}}</ref> Afterwards, he joined the [[Indian Institute of Chemical Biology]], in Kolkata, as a research fellow for his doctoral studies and submitted his thesis ''Biochemical regulation of sperm motility'', which earned him a PhD from [[Jadavpur University]] in 1990.<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P07-1433 |title=Indian fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=22 April 2017 |archive-date=5 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205154104/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P07-1433 }}</ref> He did his post-doctoral studies initially at [[California Institute of Technology]] from 1988 to 1991 as a post-doc research fellow and later, at the [[Baylor College of Medicine]], as a post-doc research associate from 1991 to 1992. On his return to India in 1992, he started his career by joining the [[National Institute of Immunology, India|National Institute of Immunology]] as a pool officer, but his stay there lasted only for two years.

In 1994, he moved to [[National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, Mohali]] as an assistant professor at the department of biotechnology where he served for over a decade and a half. During this period, he held positions as an associate professor (1999–2002) as well as a professor (2002–10), and he became head of the department in 2004. In 2010, he moved his base to New Delhi to join the [[Indian Institute of Technology]] at ''Kusuma School of Biological Sciences'' as a professor<ref name="Faculty">{{Cite web |url=http://bioschool.iitd.ac.in/people-faculty.html |title=Faculty |date=2017 |publisher=Bioschool, IIT Delhi}}</ref><ref name="Chinmoy Shankar Dey : Biological Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iitd.ac.in/content/chinmoy-shankar-dey-biological-sciences |title=Chinmoy Shankar Dey: Biological Sciences |date=2017 |publisher=IIT Delhi}}</ref> and is the head of the Central Research Facility.<ref name="Contact Us">{{Cite web |url=http://www.scfbio-iitd.res.in/crf/contact.html |title=Contact Us |date=2017 |publisher=Central Research Facility, IIT Delhi}}</ref> He leads a laboratory at IIT Delhi involved in research on [[Insulin-resistant diabetes]] and hosts a number of scholars and students.<ref name="Chinmoy S. Dey's Lab">{{Cite web |url=http://bioschool.iitd.ac.in/lab-cs-dey.html |title=Chinmoy S. Dey's Lab |date=2017 |publisher=Bioschool, IIT Delhi}}</ref> He also serves as a visiting scientist at Madras Diabetes Research Foundation (MDRF).<ref name="MDRF honours IIT Delhi professor">{{Cite web |title=MDRF honours IIT Delhi professor |date=22 July 2011 |publisher=News 18}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Dey's research has been focusing on the drug resistance of two diseases, [[leishmaniasis]] and [[diabetes]].<ref name="Indian fellow" /> His work on [[insulin resistance]] included the development of an ''[[in vitro|in-vitro]]'' model, which has potential applications in screening anti-diabetic drugs.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=446 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize}}</ref><ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | page=71 | date=1999 | access-date=26 March 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> The model, which involved insulin-resistant cultured skeletal muscle cells, earned him a US patent.<ref name="Skeletal cell model to screen anti-diabetic compounds">{{Cite web |url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/chinmoy-sankar-dey |title=Skeletal cell model to screen anti-diabetic compounds |last=Chinmoy Sankar Dey |date=30 May 2006 |publisher=Justia Patents |work=US Patent No. 7052910}}</ref> Using the model in tandem with biochemical and [[gene silencing]] methodologies, he demonstrated that [[focal adhesion kinase]]s and [[p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases]] could be used as possible drug targets.<ref name="Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize‑winner Prof. Chinmoy Sankar Dey's Work">{{Cite web |url=http://www.niscair.res.in/sciencecommunication/rndnewsletters/csirnews2k4/csirnews_15jan04.asp |title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize‑winner Prof. Chinmoy Sankar Dey's Work |date=2017 |publisher=NISCAIR}}</ref> His team identified for the first time the [[apoptosis]]-like cell death in [[Type II topoisomerase]] and suggested the [[Type II topoisomerase|enzyme]] as a possible treatment protocol for [[Leishmaniasis]].<ref name="Indian fellow" /> His findings were published in a 2005 article in ''Molecular and Biochemical Parasitology'' of [[Elsevier]].<ref name="Novobiocin induces apoptosis-like cell death in topoisomerase II over-expressing arsenite resistant Leishmania donovani">{{Cite journal |vauthors=Singh G, Jayanarayan KG, Dey CS|title=Novobiocin induces apoptosis-like cell death in topoisomerase II over-expressing arsenite resistant Leishmania donovani |journal=Mol Biochem Parasitol. |date=May 2005 |volume=141 |issue=1 |pages=57–69 |doi=10.1016/j.molbiopara.2005.01.014 |pmid=15811527}}</ref> He also proposed [[eIF4A]], a member of a set of three related [[proteins]], as a drug target to combat infection with ''[[Leishmania donovani]]'', a [[Miltefosine]]-resistant type of [[Trypanosoma|trypanosome]] causing [[leishmaniasis]].<ref name="Indian fellow" /> His work on [[myogenesis]] and [[muscular dystrophy]] showed insulin‑mediated [[dephosphorylation]] of [[PTK2]] (focal adhesion kinase) could be stopped by inhibiting the activity of the [[insulin receptor]] [[tyrosine kinase]], which was a new discovery.<ref name="Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize‑winner Prof. Chinmoy Sankar Dey's Work" /> His research has been documented in numerous articles;<ref name="Scholarly Contributions">{{Cite web |url=https://www.hindawi.com/89821536/ |title=Scholarly Contributions |date=2017 |publisher=Hindawi}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|See also "Selected bibliography" section}} [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of scientific articles, lists 90 of them.<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/researcher/39989144_Chinmoy_Sankar_Dey |title=On ResearchGate |date=2017 }}</ref> Besides this he has contributed chapters to two books,<ref name="Singh2015">{{cite book|author1=Shio Kumar Singh (editor)|author2=G. C. Majumdar, S. C. Dey, S. Saha, K. Das, D. Nath. A. Maiti, S. Dey, D. Roy|author3=S. Mitra, A. Rana, J. Chakrabarty, S. Das, A. Bhoumik, S. Banerjee, M. Mandal, B. S. Jaiswal, P. Ghosh, A. Das, D. Bhattacharyya, S. R. Dungdung (chapter authors)|title=Mammalian Endocrinology and Male Reproductive Biology|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y-KYCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA197|date=4 September 2015|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4987-2736-5|pages=197–|chapter=Role of Sperm Surface Molecules in Motility Regulation}}</ref><ref name="Singh2015-1">{{cite book|author1=Shio Kumar Singh (editor)|author2=S. C. Dey (chapter author)|title=Mammalian Endocrinology and Male Reproductive Biology|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y-KYCgAAQBAJ&pg=PR14|date=4 September 2015|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4987-2736-5|pages=14–}}</ref> and his work has drawn citations from other researchers.<ref name="SoccolPandey2016">{{cite book|author1=Vanete Thomaz Soccol|author2=Ashok Pandey|author3=Rodrigo R. Resende|title=Current Developments in Biotechnology and Bioengineering: Human and Animal Health Applications|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8HN_CwAAQBAJ&pg=PA588|date=17 September 2016|publisher=Elsevier Science|isbn=978-0-444-63671-3|pages=588–}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Studies in Natural Products Chemistry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5QRV0gT0aRMC&pg=PA427|date=15 March 2013|publisher=Newnes|isbn=978-0-444-62609-7|pages=427–}}</ref><ref name="Majumder2008">{{cite book|author=Hemanta K. Majumder|title=Drug Targets in Kinetoplastid Parasites|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rk9H6xW6Z10C&pg=PA7|date=15 September 2008|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-0-387-77570-8|pages=7–}}</ref> [[James Watson]], a recipient of the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] in 1962, cited one of Dey's papers in his 2013 lecture at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the discovery of [[double helical]] structure [[DNA]],<ref name="Faculty Profile A" /> which was later published as an article in Lancet in 2014.<ref name="Type 2 diabetes as a redox disease">{{Cite journal |title=Type 2 diabetes as a redox disease |url=http://www.thelancet.com/pdfs/journals/lancet/PIIS0140-6736(13)62365-X.pdf |journal=Lancet |date=2014 |volume=383 |issue=9919 |pages=841–43 |doi=10.1016/s0140-6736(13)62365-x|pmid=24581668 |last1=Watson |first1=James D. |s2cid=1076963 }}</ref> He also holds a [[Patent Cooperation Treaty]] and his aforementioned US patent, as well as two Indian patents, and has guided students in their master's and doctoral studies.<ref name="Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize‑winner Prof. Chinmoy Sankar Dey's Work" />

Dey was the Sectional Secretary of the 91st [[Indian Science Congress]] held in 2003; he was also associated with the organization of the ''Indo‑US Symposium on Recombinant DNA Technology and Its Application in Drug Discovery'' held at [[BITS, Pilani]] in February 1999 and the workshops on Molecular Basis of Drug Discovery and on Molecular Modeling and Pharmainformatics held at [[National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, Mohali]] in 2005.<ref name="Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize‑winner Prof. Chinmoy Sankar Dey's Work" /> He was the regional associate editor of the ''Journal of Biopharmaceutics and Biotechnology'' in 2006 and is a former member of the editorial boards of the now defunct ''Open Parasitology Journal'' of [[Bentham Science Publishers]] and ''[[Scientific Reports]]'' of [[Nature Publishing Group]].<ref name="Faculty Profile A" /> He is a reviewer for ''Molecular Biology International'', a journal of the [[Hindawi Publishing Corporation]],<ref name="Molecular Biology International">{{Cite web |url=https://www.hindawi.com/journals/mbi/reviewers/ |title=Molecular Biology International |date=2017 |publisher=Hindawi |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170327080703/https://www.hindawi.com/journals/mbi/reviewers/ |archive-date=2017-03-27 }}</ref> the ''Diabetes'' journal of the [[American Diabetes Association]], ''[[The FASEB Journal]]'', the ''Molecular Medicine'' journal, ''[[FEBS Letters]]'', the ''Journal of Molecular Cell Biology'', ''[[Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy]]'', the ''[[British Journal of Pharmacology]]'', ''[[Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology]]'', ''[[Expert Opinion on Biological Therapy]]'', the ''[[Indian Journal of Medical Research]]'', and ''[[Experimental Parasitology]]''. He has also served as an adviser or consultant to pharmaceutical companies such as Orchid Chemicals and Pharmaceutical Ltd., TCG Lifesciences (former Chembiotek Research International) and DSM Anti-Infectives.<ref name="Faculty Profile B" />

== Awards and honors ==
The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 2003.<ref name="Medical Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Medical_SCIENCES.htm |title=Medical Sciences |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130224074105/http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Medical_SCIENCES.htm |archive-date=2013-02-24 }}</ref> The same year, he also received the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]] of the [[Department of Biotechnology]],<ref name="Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development">{{Cite web |url=http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |title=Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development |date=2016 |publisher=Department of Biotechnology |access-date=26 March 2017 |archive-date=4 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304191331/http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf }}</ref> followed by the OPPI Award of the Organisation of Pharmaceutical Producers of India in 2005.<ref name="OPPI Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.niper.ac.in/oppi.htm |title=OPPI Award |date=2017 |publisher=NIPER |access-date=26 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060624231921/http://www.niper.ac.in/oppi.htm |archive-date=24 June 2006 }}</ref> He became an elected fellow of two major Indian science academies in 2007: the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |archive-date=2015-08-06 }}</ref> and the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=26 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 }}</ref> He received two honors in 2008: the CDRI Award of the [[Central Drug Research Institute]]<ref name="CDRI Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cdri.res.in/HonoursAwards.aspx |title=CDRI Award |date=2017 |publisher=Central Drug Research Institute |access-date=26 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170327081308/http://www.cdri.res.in/HonoursAwards.aspx |archive-date=27 March 2017 }}</ref> and the J. C. Bose National Fellowship of the Department of Biotechnology.<ref name="J C Bose fellowship">{{Cite web |url=http://www.niper.gov.in/jcbose_fellow.htm |title=J C Bose fellowship |date=2017 |publisher=NIPER}}</ref><ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=D |title=NASI fellows |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150717020647/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=D |archive-date=2015-07-17 }}</ref> In 2011, he was awarded the inaugural Honor Lecture Award by Madras Diabetes Research Foundation.<ref name="MDRF honours IIT Delhi professor" /> He is also a life member of the Society of Biological Chemists, India.<ref name="Faculty Profile A" />
